correctness.rationale: On the Hardy monomial basis, T_r e_{n+d}=((n+d)!/n!)r^n(e_n+c e_{n+m}); phase removal reduces epsilon^d T_r, epsilon=-log r, to (I+a S^m)D_epsilon, a=|c|>0, diagonal b_epsilon(n)=exp(-epsilon n)prod_{j=1}^d epsilon(n+j). The exact shift-form identity ||(I+aS^m)h||²=(1+a)²||h||²-a||(I-S^m)h||² yields variational norm deficit. Its unique interior maximum at epsilon n≈d has B_epsilon²=A_d²[1+(d+1)epsilon+O(epsilon²)]; shifted lattice rounding requires an explicit -C epsilon² error in lower localization bound. Rescale y=sqrt(epsilon)(n-d/epsilon), separate m residue classes and interpolate near-minimizers. Tightness and local discrete H¹ compactness give a harmonic-oscillator functional with kinetic am² and potential (1+a)²/d; its exact minimum A_d² m(1+a)sqrt(a/d) follows by completing the square. Squared norm and square root then yield first correction (d+1)/2 -m sqrt(a)/[2(1+a)sqrt d]. Independently reproduced SciPy band-matrix top eigenvalues for d=1,m=4,a=1 (coefficient→0), d=1,m=2,a=1 (→0.5), and d=2,m=2,a=1 (→1.14645), with errors decreasing as epsilon→0. Finite samples do not prove the infinite-dimensional lower bound; the interpolation/oscillator argument does.
